title: Feat: Save csv results
description:
PR https://github.com/simonpcouch/syrup/pull/14 to be able to do:

```
brulee_rss <-  syrup(
  save_csv_results = here::here(input_dir, "brulee_rss.csv"),
  interval = 10,
  {
      plan(sequential) 
      tictoc::tic()
      brulee_integer_wf <- 
        train |> 
        recipe(y ~ .) |> 
        step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) |> 
        step_integer(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
        workflow(mlp(mode = "classification") |> set_engine("brulee")) 
      brulee_integer_wf |> 
        fit_resamples(folds) |> 
        collect_metrics()
      tictoc::toc()
  }
)
here::here(input_dir, "brulee_rss.csv") |> 
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) 
```

title: rephrase "Memory Usage"
description: I really leaned on the "parallel memory usage" scope of the package at first since it only returned memory-related profiling information and that's not super useful outside of the parallelism context (as there are better, more fine-grained tools for profiling memory of single threaded code). Now that we return percent CPU as well, the discussion on the scope of the package changes a bit.

title: audit `pct_cpu` values on macOS
description:
Related to #1. The distributions of `pct_cpu` values, intended to measure CPU usage, are weird on MacOS. Here's an example that distributes a set of linear regression fits across 5 cores using forking: 

``` r
library(syrup)
#> Loading required package: bench
```

``` r
library(future)
library(tidymodels)
 
# explicitly enable forking in RStudio, otherwise future will complain
rlang::local_options(parallelly.fork.enable = TRUE)

# use 5 workers via forking
plan(multicore, workers = 5)

# wrap model resampling in `syrup()` to profile CPU usage
res_mem <- syrup({
  res <-
    fit_resamples(
      linear_reg(),
      outcome ~ .,
      vfold_cv(sim_regression(1000000))
    )
})
```

The distribution of `pct_cpu` values seems spot on (except they need to be multiplied by 100, woops) when I run it on Linux. Most of the time, most R sessions are using very little CPU, though each child of the parent process briefly hits 100% while training models:


```r
hist(res_mem$pct_cpu)
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/iKu41Tg.png)<!-- -->

<sup>Created on 2024-06-24 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>


Here's what the distribution looks like when I run it on macOS, though:


![](https://i.imgur.com/06Abf7f.png)<!-- -->

Trying to figure out if that 2.4% approximates something that's useful for debugging... this Macbook has 10 cores.

title: look into providing CPU usage
description:
From @topepo:

> ...can you get other process parameters (like cpu usage)?

This is definitely something I'd love to have available. From my understanding, the ps package doesn't include tools for measuring e.g. "% CPU" in Activity Monitor. If we can find a safe way to grab that information, we ought to.

title: include time that a snapshot was taken at
description:
From @topepo:

> One other thing: getting the actual times would be good. My initial application was looking at how fast workers finished for different tasks.

Currently, `id` is just a counter. We could either replace it with the time that the snapshot was taken or include both.
